sentences.text: Austroraptor was a large, bipedal carnivore measuring between 5 and 6 meters in length and weighing between 300 and 520 kilograms.
This predator possessed a low, elongated skull measuring 80 centimeters in length, which was more elongated than those of other dromaeosaurs.
Its mouth contained conical, non-serrated teeth with fluted enamel, a feature compared to those of spinosaurids.
A notable feature of Austroraptor was its relatively short forearms compared to most members of its group.
Austroraptor is one of the largest known paravian dinosaurs, comparable in size only to large dromaeosaurids like Achillobator and Utahraptor.
It is the largest dromaeosaurid discovered in the Southern Hemisphere, surpassed only by Achillobator, Dakotaraptor, and Utahraptor.
The holotype specimen of Austroraptor was found in the Bajo de Santa Rosa locality within the Allen Formation in Río Negro, Argentina.
This fossil was collected in 2002 by Fernando Novas's team from the Museo Argentino de Ciencias Naturales near Lamarque, Río Negro Province.
The species Austroraptor cabazai was formally named and described in 2008 by Fernando Emilio Novas and colleagues.
There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Austroraptor known to science.
Researchers suggest that unenlagiines like Austroraptor had superior running and pursuit predation capabilities compared to other dromaeosaurids.

In 2021, Brum and colleagues proposed that Austroraptor likely consumed fish as a significant or primary part of its diet, based on its non-serrated conical teeth resembling those of piscivorous tetrapods.
Austroraptor shared its paleoenvironment with early mammals, pterosaurs, and the titanosaurs Saltasaurus and Rocasaurus, which may have served as prey for this dromaeosaurid.
The discovery of Austroraptor suggests that large coelurosaurs became common in the Late Cretaceous after the dominance of carcharodontosaurids declined.
Austroraptor represents a previously unknown lineage of large predators in the late Cretaceous fauna, which was dominated mainly by abelisaurids.
Cladistic analysis places Austroraptor within the subfamily Unenlagiinae of the family Dromaeosauridae.
Austroraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous period in the Allen Formation of Argentina.
The animal lived during the Campanian and Maastrichtian stages of the Late Cretaceous period.
Thomas R. Holtz Jr. estimated that Austroraptor lived between 78 and 66 million years ago.
The time range for Austroraptor is the Maastrichtian, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
The specimen was found in terrestrial sediments deposited during the Maastrichtian stage of the Cretaceous period, approximately 70 million years ago.
Austroraptor is the youngest record of dromaeosaurids found in Gondwana.
Some researchers have hypothesized that the holotype specimen of Austroraptor might be a paleontological chimera, though this remains unproven.
